passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and tell him that this is what the LORD says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD said, "Go to Pharaoh."
The LORD told Moses to speak to Pharaoh.
The LORD said, "This is what I say."
The LORD said, "Let My people go."
The LORD said, "Let them go so they may worship Me."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֹּ֖א אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־ עַמִּ֖י וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי׃

passages.text: But if you refuse to let them go, I will plague your whole country with frogs.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Pharaoh through Moses.
God gave Pharaoh a command.
God said, "Let My people go."
God warned Pharaoh.
God said, "If you refuse to let My people go, I will punish you."
God said, "I will send a plague of frogs."
God said, "Frogs will cover your whole country."
passages.original: וְאִם־ מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לְשַׁלֵּ֑חַ הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֗י נֹגֵ֛ף אֶת־ כָּל־ גְּבוּלְךָ֖ בַּֽצְפַרְדְּעִֽים׃

passages.text: The Nile will teem with frogs, and they will come into your palace and up to your bedroom and onto your bed, into the houses of your officials and your people, and into your ovens and kneading bowls.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God sent Moses to Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
God told Moses to warn Pharaoh.
God said He would send a plague if Pharaoh refused to let the Israelites go.
God said the Nile River would fill with frogs.
Frogs would come out of the river.
Frogs would enter Pharaoh’s palace.
Frogs would go into Pharaoh’s bedroom.
Frogs would get onto Pharaoh’s bed.
Frogs would enter the houses of Pharaoh’s officials.
Frogs would enter the houses of the Egyptian people.
Frogs would go into their ovens.
Frogs would go into their kneading bowls.
passages.original: וְשָׁרַ֣ץ הַיְאֹר֮ צְפַרְדְּעִים֒ וְעָלוּ֙ וּבָ֣אוּ בְּבֵיתֶ֔ךָ וּבַחֲדַ֥ר מִשְׁכָּבְךָ֖ וְעַל־ מִטָּתֶ֑ךָ וּבְבֵ֤ית עֲבָדֶ֙יךָ֙ וּבְעַמֶּ֔ךָ וּבְתַנּוּרֶ֖יךָ וּבְמִשְׁאֲרוֹתֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: The frogs will come up on you and your people and all your officials.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Pharaoh through Moses.
God warned Pharaoh about a plague of frogs.
God said the frogs will come up on you, Pharaoh.
The frogs will come up on your people.
The frogs will come up on all your officials.
passages.original: וּבְכָ֥ה וּֽבְעַמְּךָ֖ וּבְכָל־ עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ יַעֲל֖וּ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִֽים׃

passages.text: And the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers and canals and ponds, and cause the frogs to come up onto the land of Egypt.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to Aaron.
Aaron is Moses’ brother.
Aaron serves as Moses’ helper.
The LORD told Moses what Aaron must do.
Aaron must stretch out his hand.
Aaron must hold his staff in his hand.
Aaron must stretch out his hand over the rivers.
Aaron must stretch out his hand over the canals.
Aaron must stretch out his hand over the ponds.
Aaron must bring frogs up from the water.
Aaron must bring the frogs onto the land of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה֒ אֱמֹ֣ר אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֗ן נְטֵ֤ה אֶת־ יָדְךָ֙ בְּמַטֶּ֔ךָ עַל־ הַ֨נְּהָרֹ֔ת עַל־ הַיְאֹרִ֖ים וְעַל־ הָאֲגַמִּ֑ים וְהַ֥עַל אֶת־ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֖ים עַל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Aaron was Moses’ brother.
Aaron served as God’s chosen helper.
Aaron stretched out his hand.
He held his staff in his hand.
He stretched his hand over the waters of Egypt.
The waters included rivers, canals, and ponds.
Frogs came up from the waters.
The frogs covered the land of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֤ט אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶת־ יָד֔וֹ עַ֖ל מֵימֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם וַתַּ֙עַל֙ הַצְּפַרְדֵּ֔עַ וַתְּכַ֖ס אֶת־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: But the magicians did the same thing by their magic arts, and they also brought frogs up onto the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
The magicians of Egypt used their secret arts.
They did the same thing as Aaron.
They brought frogs up onto the land of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־ כֵ֥ן הַֽחֲרְטֻמִּ֖ים בְּלָטֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּעֲל֥וּ אֶת־ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֖ים עַל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “Pray to the LORD to take the frogs away from me and my people. Then I will let your people go, that they may sacrifice to the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron.
Moses and Aaron were leaders of the Israelites.
Pharaoh spoke to Moses and Aaron.
Pharaoh said, “Pray to the LORD for me.”
Pharaoh asked them to ask the LORD to remove the frogs.
Pharaoh wanted the frogs taken away from himself and from his people.
Pharaoh said, “If you do this, I will let your people go.”
Pharaoh said, “Then your people may offer sacrifices to the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א פַרְעֹ֜ה לְמֹשֶׁ֣ה וּֽלְאַהֲרֹ֗ן וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַעְתִּ֣ירוּ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה וְיָסֵר֙ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֔ים מִמֶּ֖נִּי וּמֵֽעַמִּ֑י וַאֲשַׁלְּחָה֙ אֶת־ הָעָ֔ם וְיִזְבְּח֖וּ לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Moses said to Pharaoh, “You may have the honor over me. When shall I pray for you and your officials and your people that the frogs (except for those in the Nile) may be taken away from you and your houses?”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to Pharaoh.
Moses was a prophet and leader of the Israelites.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Moses said, "You may choose the time."
Moses asked, "When should I pray for you?"
Moses included Pharaoh’s officials and people in his question.
Moses said he would pray for the frogs to be removed from Pharaoh, his officials, and his people.
Moses said the frogs would be taken away from Pharaoh’s houses.
Moses said only the frogs in the Nile would remain.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה לְפַרְעֹה֮ הִתְפָּאֵ֣ר עָלַי֒ לְמָתַ֣י׀ אַעְתִּ֣יר לְךָ֗ וְלַעֲבָדֶ֙יךָ֙ וּֽלְעַמְּךָ֔ לְהַכְרִית֙ הַֽצֲפַרְדְּעִ֔ים מִמְּךָ֖ וּמִבָּתֶּ֑יךָ רַ֥ק בַּיְאֹ֖ר תִּשָּׁאַֽרְנָה׃

passages.text: “Tomorrow,” Pharaoh answered. “May it be as you say,” Moses replied, “so that you may know that there is no one like the LORD our God.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh spoke to Moses.
Pharaoh said, “Tomorrow.”
Moses replied to Pharaoh.
Moses said, “It will happen as you said.”
Moses explained the reason.
Moses said, “This will happen so you will know something important.”
Moses said, “There is no one like the LORD our God.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְמָחָ֑ר וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ כִּדְבָ֣רְךָ֔ לְמַ֣עַן תֵּדַ֔ע כִּי־ אֵ֖ין כַּיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: The frogs will depart from you and your houses and your officials and your people; they will remain only in the Nile.”
passages.sermon:
God sent a plague of frogs against Egypt.
Moses spoke to Pharaoh.
Moses said the frogs would leave Pharaoh.
The frogs would leave Pharaoh’s houses.
The frogs would leave Pharaoh’s officials.
The frogs would leave Pharaoh’s people.
Only the frogs in the Nile would remain.
passages.original: וְסָר֣וּ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֗ים מִמְּךָ֙ וּמִבָּ֣תֶּ֔יךָ וּמֵעֲבָדֶ֖יךָ וּמֵעַמֶּ֑ךָ רַ֥ק בַּיְאֹ֖ר תִּשָּׁאַֽרְנָה׃

passages.text: After Moses and Aaron had left Pharaoh, Moses cried out to the LORD for help with the frogs that He had brought against Pharaoh.
passages.sermon:
Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh.
Moses prayed to the LORD.
Moses asked the LORD for help with the frogs.
The LORD had sent the frogs against Pharaoh.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֥א מֹשֶׁ֛ה וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן מֵעִ֣ם פַּרְעֹ֑ה וַיִּצְעַ֤ק מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה עַל־ דְּבַ֥ר הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֖ים אֲשֶׁר־ שָׂ֥ם לְפַרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: And the LORD did as Moses requested, and the frogs in the houses, the courtyards, and the fields died.
passages.sermon:
The LORD listened to Moses.
The LORD acted as Moses asked.
The frogs died.
The frogs died in the houses.
The frogs died in the courtyards.
The frogs died in the fields.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ יְהוָ֖ה כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיָּמֻ֙תוּ֙ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֔ים מִן־ הַבָּתִּ֥ים מִן־ הַחֲצֵרֹ֖ת וּמִן־ הַשָּׂדֹֽת׃

passages.text: They were piled into countless heaps, and there was a terrible stench in the land.
passages.sermon: The people gathered the dead frogs into large piles.\r\nThey made many heaps of frogs.\r\nA terrible smell filled the land.
passages.original: וַיִּצְבְּר֥וּ אֹתָ֖ם חֳמָרִ֣ם חֳמָרִ֑ם וַתִּבְאַ֖שׁ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: When Pharaoh saw that there was relief, however, he hardened his heart and would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh saw that there was relief from the plague.
Pharaoh hardened his heart.
Pharaoh did not listen to Moses and Aaron.
The LORD had said this would happen.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא פַּרְעֹ֗ה כִּ֤י הָֽיְתָה֙ הָֽרְוָחָ֔ה וְהַכְבֵּד֙ אֶת־ לִבּ֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵהֶ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth, that it may turn into swarms of gnats throughout the land of Egypt.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD told Moses what to do.
The LORD said, “Tell Aaron this command.
Aaron is Moses’ brother.
Aaron must stretch out his staff.
Aaron must strike the dust of the earth with his staff.
The dust will become gnats.
Gnats will appear everywhere in the land of Egypt.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה֒ אֱמֹר֙ אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֔ן נְטֵ֣ה אֶֽת־ מַטְּךָ֔ וְהַ֖ךְ אֶת־ עֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהָיָ֥ה לְכִנִּ֖ם בְּכָל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: This they did, and when Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the earth, gnats came upon man and beast. All the dust of the earth turned into gnats throughout the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Aaron was Moses’ brother.
Aaron obeyed God’s command.
Aaron stretched out his hand.
Aaron held his staff in his hand.
Aaron struck the dust of the earth with his staff.
Gnats appeared on people.
Gnats appeared on animals.
All the dust in Egypt became gnats.
Gnats covered the whole land of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־ כֵ֗ן וַיֵּט֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן אֶת־ יָד֤וֹ בְמַטֵּ֙הוּ֙ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־ עֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֔רֶץ וַתְּהִי֙ הַכִּנָּ֔ם בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָ֑ה כָּל־ עֲפַ֥ר הָאָ֛רֶץ הָיָ֥ה כִנִּ֖ים בְּכָל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: The magicians tried to produce gnats using their magic arts, but they could not. And the gnats remained on man and beast.
passages.sermon:
The magicians served Pharaoh in Egypt.
The magicians used their secret arts.
The magicians tried to make gnats appear.
The magicians could not make gnats appear.
Gnats stayed on people.
Gnats stayed on animals.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ־ כֵ֨ן הַחַרְטֻמִּ֧ים בְּלָטֵיהֶ֛ם לְהוֹצִ֥יא אֶת־ הַכִּנִּ֖ים וְלֹ֣א יָכֹ֑לוּ וַתְּהִי֙ הַכִּנָּ֔ם בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָֽה׃

passages.text: “This is the finger of God,” the magicians said to Pharaoh. But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
passages.sermon:
The magicians spoke to Pharaoh.
They said, “This is the finger of God.”
Pharaoh’s heart became hard.
Pharaoh did not listen to the magicians.
The LORD had said this would happen.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ הַֽחַרְטֻמִּים֙ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה אֶצְבַּ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִ֑וא וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק לֵב־ פַּרְעֹה֙ וְלֹֽא־ שָׁמַ֣ע אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Get up early in the morning, and when Pharaoh goes out to the water, stand before him and tell him that this is what the LORD says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD told Moses to get up early in the morning.
Pharaoh is the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh goes out to the water in the morning.
The LORD told Moses to stand before Pharaoh.
The LORD told Moses to speak to Pharaoh.
Moses must say, “This is what the LORD says.”
The LORD says, “Let My people go.”
The LORD’s people are the Israelites.
The LORD says, “Let them go so they may worship Me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֗ה הַשְׁכֵּ֤ם בַּבֹּ֙קֶר֙ וְהִתְיַצֵּב֙ לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה הִנֵּ֖ה יוֹצֵ֣א הַמָּ֑יְמָה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שַׁלַּ֥ח עַמִּ֖י וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי׃

passages.text: But if you will not let My people go, I will send swarms of flies upon you and your officials and your people and your houses. The houses of the Egyptians and even the ground where they stand will be full of flies.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Pharaoh through Moses.
God said, “If you do not let My people go, I will act against you.
I will send swarms of flies against you.
I will send flies against your officials.
I will send flies against your people.
I will send flies into your houses.
The houses of the Egyptians will be filled with flies.
The ground where the Egyptians stand will also be covered with flies.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י אִם־ אֵינְךָ֮ מְשַׁלֵּ֣חַ אֶת־ עַמִּי֒ הִנְנִי֩ מַשְׁלִ֨יחַ בְּךָ֜ וּבַעֲבָדֶ֧יךָ וּֽבְעַמְּךָ֛ וּבְבָתֶּ֖יךָ אֶת־ הֶעָרֹ֑ב וּמָ֨לְא֜וּ בָּתֵּ֤י מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ אֶת־ הֶ֣עָרֹ֔ב וְגַ֥ם הָאֲדָמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־ הֵ֥ם עָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: But on that day I will give special treatment to the land of Goshen, where My people live; no swarms of flies will be found there. In this way you will know that I, the LORD, am in the land.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke about the land of Goshen.
Goshen is where the LORD’s people live.
On that day, the LORD will treat Goshen differently.
No swarms of flies will be in Goshen.
The LORD will do this so you will know something.
You will know that the LORD is present in the land.
passages.original: וְהִפְלֵיתִי֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא אֶת־ אֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֗שֶׁן אֲשֶׁ֤ר עַמִּי֙ עֹמֵ֣ד עָלֶ֔יהָ לְבִלְתִּ֥י הֱיֽוֹת־ שָׁ֖ם עָרֹ֑ב לְמַ֣עַן תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: I will make a distinction between My people and your people. This sign will take place tomorrow.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Pharaoh through Moses.
God said He would act.
God would make a clear difference between His people and Pharaoh’s people.
God’s people were the Israelites.
Pharaoh’s people were the Egyptians.
God would show this difference as a sign.
This sign would happen the next day.
passages.original: וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י פְדֻ֔ת בֵּ֥ין עַמִּ֖י וּבֵ֣ין עַמֶּ֑ךָ לְמָחָ֥ר יִהְיֶ֖ה הָאֹ֥ת הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: And the LORD did so. Thick swarms of flies poured into Pharaoh’s palace and into the houses of his officials. Throughout Egypt the land was ruined by swarms of flies.
passages.sermon:
The LORD acted as He said.
Thick swarms of flies entered Pharaoh’s palace.
Thick swarms of flies entered the houses of Pharaoh’s officials.
Swarms of flies filled all of Egypt.
The land of Egypt was ruined because of the swarms of flies.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ יְהוָה֙ כֵּ֔ן וַיָּבֹא֙ עָרֹ֣ב כָּבֵ֔ד בֵּ֥יתָה פַרְעֹ֖ה וּבֵ֣ית עֲבָדָ֑יו וּבְכָל־ אֶ֧רֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם תִּשָּׁחֵ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ מִפְּנֵ֥י הֶעָרֹֽב׃

passages.text: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “Go, sacrifice to your God within this land.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron.
Moses and Aaron were leaders of the Israelites.
Pharaoh spoke to them.
Pharaoh said, “Go.”
Pharaoh said, “Sacrifice to your God.”
Pharaoh said, “Do it here in this land.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֣א פַרְעֹ֔ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֖ה וּֽלְאַהֲרֹ֑ן וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְכ֛וּ זִבְח֥וּ לֵֽאלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: But Moses replied, “It would not be right to do that, because the sacrifices we offer to the LORD our God would be detestable to the Egyptians. If we offer sacrifices that are detestable before the Egyptians, will they not stone us?
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to Pharaoh.
Moses said, “It is not right for us to do this.
We cannot sacrifice here in Egypt.
The animals we sacrifice to the LORD our God are detestable to the Egyptians.
If we sacrifice what the Egyptians hate, and they see us do it, they will stone us.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה לֹ֤א נָכוֹן֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת כֵּ֔ן כִּ֚י תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת מִצְרַ֔יִם נִזְבַּ֖ח לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ הֵ֣ן נִזְבַּ֞ח אֶת־ תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת מִצְרַ֛יִם לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א יִסְקְלֻֽנוּ׃

passages.text: We must make a three-day journey into the wilderness and sacrifice to the LORD our God as He commands us.”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to Pharaoh.
Moses said the Israelites must travel for three days.
They must go into the wilderness.
They must offer sacrifices there.
They must sacrifice to the LORD, who is their God.
They must do this as the LORD commands them.
passages.original: דֶּ֚רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים נֵלֵ֖ךְ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְזָבַ֙חְנוּ֙ לַֽיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר יֹאמַ֥ר אֵלֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Pharaoh answered, “I will let you go and sacrifice to the LORD your God in the wilderness, but you must not go very far. Now pray for me.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh spoke to Moses.
Pharaoh said, "I will let you go."
Pharaoh said, "You may sacrifice to the LORD your God."
Pharaoh said, "You must do this in the wilderness."
Pharaoh said, "Do not go very far away."
Pharaoh said, "Pray for me."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֗ה אָנֹכִ֞י אֲשַׁלַּ֤ח אֶתְכֶם֙ וּזְבַחְתֶּ֞ם לַיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר רַ֛ק הַרְחֵ֥ק לֹא־ תַרְחִ֖יקוּ לָלֶ֑כֶת הַעְתִּ֖ירוּ בַּעֲדִֽי׃

passages.text: “As soon as I leave you,” Moses said, “I will pray to the LORD, so that tomorrow the swarms of flies will depart from Pharaoh and his officials and his people. But Pharaoh must not act deceitfully again by refusing to let the people go and sacrifice to the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Moses spoke to Pharaoh.
Moses said, “I am about to leave you now.
I will pray to the LORD.
The LORD is the God of the Hebrews.
Tomorrow, the swarms of flies will leave Pharaoh.
The flies will also leave Pharaoh’s officials.
The flies will also leave Pharaoh’s people.
But Pharaoh must not deceive us again.
Pharaoh must not refuse to let the people go.
The people must be allowed to sacrifice to the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י יוֹצֵ֤א מֵֽעִמָּךְ֙ וְהַעְתַּרְתִּ֣י אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה וְסָ֣ר הֶעָרֹ֗ב מִפַּרְעֹ֛ה מֵעֲבָדָ֥יו וּמֵעַמּ֖וֹ מָחָ֑ר רַ֗ק אַל־ יֹסֵ֤ף פַּרְעֹה֙ הָתֵ֔ל לְבִלְתִּי֙ שַׁלַּ֣ח אֶת־ הָעָ֔ם לִזְבֹּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to the LORD, and the LORD did as Moses requested. He removed the swarms of flies from Pharaoh and his officials and his people; not one fly remained.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet and leader of the Israelites.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Moses left Pharaoh.
Moses prayed to the LORD.
The LORD listened to Moses.
The LORD did what Moses asked.
The LORD removed the swarms of flies.
He took the flies away from Pharaoh.
He took the flies away from Pharaoh’s officials.
He took the flies away from Pharaoh’s people.
Not one fly remained.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֥א מֹשֶׁ֖ה מֵעִ֣ם פַּרְעֹ֑ה וַיֶּעְתַּ֖ר אֶל־ יְהוָֽה׃ וַיַּ֤עַשׂ יְהוָה֙ כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיָּ֙סַר֙ הֶעָרֹ֔ב מִפַּרְעֹ֖ה מֵעֲבָדָ֣יו וּמֵעַמּ֑וֹ לֹ֥א נִשְׁאַ֖ר אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: But Pharaoh hardened his heart this time as well, and he would not let the people go.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh made his heart stubborn again.
He refused to change his mind.
He did not let the people of Israel go.
passages.original: וַיַּכְבֵּ֤ד פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת־ לִבּ֔וֹ גַּ֖ם בַּפַּ֣עַם הַזֹּ֑את וְלֹ֥א שִׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־ הָעָֽם׃פ
